# Caveman Ecosystem Documentation

> Official documentation for the Caveman ecosystem.


> Note: This documentation portal is generated based on commit 99a9aa2f5a45097fc3563febea7d0baf64407441 of the original repo on August 19, 2026. Please refer to the original repo (https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman) for the latest updates.


## Caveman
> Caveman - Original skill making agents read and write less.

- [Caveman technical documentation](/docs/caveman/): This manual explains the public Caveman repository from installation through runtime behavior.

### How To
- [Install and update](/docs/caveman/how-to/install-and-update): Caveman ships a response-skill installer and a separate local-runtime CLI.
- [Extending Caveman](/docs/caveman/how-to/extending): Extensions should preserve original input on uncertainty, keep recovery exact, and label measurements by evidence source.

### Explanation
- [Product model](/docs/caveman/explanation/product-model): Caveman has two local adoption paths.
- [Architecture](/docs/caveman/explanation/architecture): Caveman's local runtime is a set of small processes joined by documented files, stdio, loopback HTTP, and Model Context Protocol (MCP).
- [Agent wrapping](/docs/caveman/explanation/agent-wrapping): Agent wrapping starts an existing coding agent with local Caveman endpoints, hooks, skills, and recovery tools.
- [Compression Engine](/docs/caveman/explanation/engine): Caveman Engine is a local Go library and command-line runtime for reducing model context.
- [TOON and pixel context](/docs/caveman/explanation/toon-and-pixel): TOON and pixel are optional context encodings.
- [Cache planner and trajectory rewriter](/docs/caveman/explanation/cache-and-rewriter): Caveman includes two independent optimization systems:
- [Context recovery](/docs/caveman/explanation/context-recovery): Caveman Context Recovery, abbreviated CCR, stores exact original bytes behind a short reference.
- [Local proxy and providers](/docs/caveman/explanation/proxy-and-providers): Local proxy presents provider-compatible HTTP routes on loopback, applies configured local transforms, forwards requests to provider endpoints, and...
- [Security and privacy](/docs/caveman/explanation/security-and-privacy): Caveman local runtime processes prompts, tool output, source code, provider credentials, and browser state.
- [Accounting and evidence](/docs/caveman/explanation/accounting-and-evidence): Caveman labels numbers by how they were produced.
- [Testing and benchmarks](/docs/caveman/explanation/testing-and-benchmarks): Repository uses language-specific tests plus cross-package verification.

### Reference
- [CLI reference](/docs/caveman/reference/cli-reference): `caveman` and `cave` invoke the same command-line program.
- [Configuration](/docs/caveman/reference/configuration): Caveman has two configuration layers:
- [Local tools](/docs/caveman/reference/local-tools): Caveman ships local tools for recovery, memory, browser context, and large command output.
- [Skills, hooks, and plugins](/docs/caveman/reference/skills-hooks-and-plugins): Caveman integrates through response skills, lifecycle hooks, and agent-specific plugins.
- [Exploration and delegation](/docs/caveman/reference/exploration-and-delegation): Broad repository search can consume main agent context before editing begins.
- [SDKs and public packages](/docs/caveman/reference/sdks-and-packages): Repository contains standalone packages for application integration, agent construction, schemas, evaluation, user-interface labels, provider price...
- [Glossary](/docs/caveman/reference/glossary): Browser-provided semantic representation of page roles, names, states, and relationships.
